output.answer: Wells Fargo's most recent settlement is an October 2026 multistate deal in which it agreed with Merrill Lynch to pay about $4.4 million in restitution, fines and costs over unreasonable retail brokerage commissions charged on roughly 228,243 equity transactions from September 30, 2020 to October 1, 2025 (Wells Fargo's share of the excessive commissions was nearly $3.9 million). Earlier in 2026 it reached an $85 million settlement of the securities class action over its 'Diverse Search' hiring practices (final judgment entered September 11, 2026), a $110 million settlement of consolidated discrimination lawsuits alleging sham interviews with minority candidates and lending discrimination (final approval May 18, 2026, including a $100 million borrower assistance fund), and a $50 million settlement over its role in the J&J Consulting Ponzi scheme, which had a final approval hearing set for November 12, 2026; it also agreed to pay more than $56 million in a class action over misreported CARES Act forbearances. In January 2025 its brokerage units paid $35 million of a $60 million SEC cash-sweep settlement (with Merrill Lynch paying $25 million). Going back further, between 2016 and 2026 Wells Fargo paid over $8 billion in penalties and consumer redress across regulator actions, including the $185 million fake-accounts settlement (2016), the $1 billion CFPB/OCC auto-loan and mortgage settlement (2018), the $3 billion DOJ/SEC resolution (2020), and the $3.7 billion CFPB order (2022).
caveats: The $50 million J&J Ponzi-scheme settlement had only preliminary court approval as of July 9, 2026, with a final approval hearing scheduled for November 12, 2026, so it could still be modified.

The October 2026 $4.4 million figure is a 'settlement agreement in principle' announced by state regulators; Wells Fargo neither admitted nor denied the findings, and the multistate figure combines Wells Fargo and Merrill Lynch payments.

The $85 million securities class action settlement and the $110 million discrimination settlement are related but distinct cases over the same sham-interview allegations; the $110 million figure and its terms come from news coverage of the May 18, 2026 final approval.

The historical cumulative figure (over $8 billion in penalties and redress 2016-2026, including the $185M, $1B, $3B and $3.7B resolutions) is drawn from a secondary legal overview; the underlying regulator press pages could not be retrieved to confirm the amounts directly.

output.question: What settlements has Wells Fargo reached?

key_facts.fact: State securities regulators secured a $4.4 million settlement agreement in principle with Wells Fargo and Merrill Lynch over unreasonable commissions on more than 256,000 equity transactions; Wells Fargo's share covered approximately 228,243 transactions totaling nearly $3.9 million in excessive commissions from Sept. 30, 2020 to Oct. 1, 2025, with restitution plus 6% interest.

Under the Massachusetts consent order (lead state for the multistate group), Wells Fargo agreed to pay a $38,000 administrative fine and at least $79,761.45 in restitution plus 6% interest to affected Massachusetts customers, and was censured, without admitting or denying the findings.

The securities class action over Wells Fargo's Diverse Search hiring initiative (SEB Investment Management AB and West Palm Beach Firefighters' Pension Fund v. Wells Fargo, N.D. Cal. 3:22-cv-03811) settled for $85,000,000 in cash; the court granted final approval on May 21, 2026 and entered final judgment on September 11, 2026.

Wells Fargo agreed to a $110 million settlement of consolidated lawsuits alleging discriminatory hiring (sham interviews with minority candidates) and lending discrimination, which creates a $100 million borrower assistance fund for low-to-moderate income mortgage borrowers; final approval was granted May 18, 2026.

A court granted preliminary approval on July 9, 2026 of a $50 million settlement with Wells Fargo in the J&J Consulting Ponzi scheme litigation, over claims the bank enabled the scheme through a lawyer's trust (IOLTA) account; final approval hearing set for November 12, 2026.

Wells Fargo agreed to pay more than $56 million ($56.85 million) to settle a class action alleging it violated the Fair Credit Reporting Act by failing to accurately report CARES Act mortgage forbearances, harming consumers' credit scores; the bank admitted no wrongdoing.

Wells Fargo Clearing Services ($28 million) and Wells Fargo Advisors Financial Network ($7 million) agreed to pay a combined $60 million with Merrill Lynch ($25 million) to settle SEC charges over compliance failures in their cash sweep programs.

Between 2016 and 2026 Wells Fargo and its affiliates paid more than $8 billion in penalties and consumer redress across CFPB, OCC, DOJ, SEC, FINRA and Federal Reserve actions, including the $185 million fake-accounts settlement (2016), the $1 billion CFPB/OCC auto-insurance and mortgage settlement (2018), the $3 billion DOJ/SEC criminal and civil resolution (2020), and the $3.7 billion CFPB order (2022).
